newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea spy may be among crew of drug ship.
newsitem.headline: North Korea spy may be among crew of drug ship.

text.p: One of 17 crewmembers aboard a North Korean freighter raided in a huge drug haul last week may be a North Korean spy, Japanese newspapers reported on Tuesday.

Quoting police sources, the dailies Tokyo Shimbun and Sankei Shimbun said Japanese investigators believe the North Korean belonged to an intelligence unit within North Korea's military or ruling Korea Workers' (communist) Party.
The dailies said intelligence equipment including a table of random secret codes were also found on the North Korean-registered Ji Song-2.
The freighter is being held at the western Japan port of Shimonoseki.
A spokesman for Miyazaki Prefectural Police, in charge of the investigation, declined to comment on the reports.

Last week, Japanese police arrested three North Korean nationals on suspicion of smuggling a huge cache of amphetamines in cargo labelled as honey on the 1,499-tonne freighter. The ship left North Korea's Nanpo port on April 5.

Investigators found 70 kg (154 lb) of amphetamines with a street value estimated at 11.9 billion yen ($95 million) in cargo from the ship after it docked at the port of Hososhima on the Pacific coast of the southern main island of Kyushu. The ship later steamed to Shimonoseki.
The dailies said Japanese authorities were investigating whether the Pyongyang government was involved in what could be the biggest ever drug smuggling case involving North Koreans.
Japanese intelligence sources told Reuters on Monday that they believe the cash-strapped North Korean government may have been behind the drug smuggling operation.
They said North Korea, gripped by famine after two consecutive years of flooding, may have been cornered into taking illegal steps to earn foreign exchange.
